Leveraged Fund Decay

A daily-reset fund with leverage L does not return L times its benchmark over time. The gap has three parts:
  • Compounding: the path effect of resetting every day. It costs about (L² − L)/2 × variance a year, so it is negative when the benchmark chops and can be positive in a steady trend. An inverse fund pays more than a long fund of the same size: −3x pays twice what 3x pays.
  • Financing: a long fund borrows (L − 1) times its assets and an inverse fund holds (1 − L) times its assets in cash, at the 3-month T-bill rate. Long funds pay it and inverse funds earn it. VIX funds are measured against VXX, which earns no interest, so their collateral earns the full rate.
  • Fees and tracking: the rest: expense ratio, swap spreads, and the gap between the fund's own index and the ETF used as its benchmark. Tracking error shows how good that match is.

By VX regime
Each day's fund return is tagged with the VX regime at the previous close (M2 against M1: stress backwardation more than 8% below, shallow backwardation 0.5% to 8% below, flat within 0.5%, shallow contango 0.5% to 3% above, normal 3% to 8%, deep above 8%), so the tag is known in advance.
